success_patterns: Translate each option into its full quantified claim before ranking it. The exact scope mattered repeatedly: generic versus universal, almost every versus every, all parameters versus sufficiently large parameters, existence versus uniqueness, and per-time-interval bounds versus bounds uniform for all time.

Verify each precise quantitative modifier against the applicable result rather than choosing by apparent strength. Successful choices preserved the supported exponent, endpoint strictness, constant dependence, inequality direction, and regularity or norm; stronger-looking rates or added clauses were not accepted without support.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already covers exact quantifiers and quantitative comparisons. These trajectories additionally make the order and scope of nested limits a decisive distinction, so a focused operational reminder addresses that gap without repeating a generic exactness rule.

edits.content: - **Preserve the order and scope of nested limits.** Read them from the inside out: a limit in a truncation parameter after a time limit is not automatically interchangeable with a time limsup, a time limit uniform in the truncation parameter, or convergence of the untruncated series. Likewise, bounds valid separately on each finite time interval do not imply bounds uniform over all time.
